title: One complete tracking round
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $y$, and let $b$ be a Boolean tag satisfying the boundary conditions for the input-head position of $c$. Assign a natural number $n_i$ to each of the $2(1+k)$ counter indices, and suppose their binary representations all have length at most $W$. There is a time $	au$ with $0<\tau\le 2W+4$ such that at every integer time $j$ with $0<j<\tau$, the tracking machine is in its bank phase; at time $\tau$ it is at the canonical configuration for the one-step successor of $c$, with a valid boundary tag and each counter updated by one exactly when its index is selected by the actual source-head displacement vector.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$b$ satisfies the boundary-tag conditions at $c$'s input-head position
there is a natural counter value for each of the $2(1+k)$ indices
each counter's binary representation has length at most $W$
replaced: Let $c$ be a source configuration with a valid position tag bit, and let movement counts be given whose binary representations fit a common width $W$. Then there is a strictly positive time $\tau \le 2W + 4$ such that: every intermediate time strictly between $0$ and $\tau$ is in the bank phase, not at the anchor; and at $\tau$ the tracking host is back at the canonical seam for the stepped source configuration, with a valid new tag and with exactly the clamped displacement counts advanced. Source output is suppressed and every counter head is restored.
